name: plan-review-agent-reconciliation
body:
Provenance and decisions for the plan-review agent-prompt reconciliation on the `coverage-spec-delta` change-set.

SOURCE. In reconciliation mode the coordinator directed: extend the existing plan-coverage spec with the plan-review agent's behaviour — (1) verify coverage DETERMINISTICALLY via the binary's delta coverage check and treat any gap as blocking feedback; then (2) review each plan node (phase/task/planned node) semantically against the spec delta with an explicit less-code bias (prefer `deletes` over `modifies`, `modifies` over `creates`, fewer planned nodes; flag speculative/unnecessary additions). In particular, removing a solution node or an `implemented-by` edge should almost always result in removal of the code it pointed at (a `deletes` task); a `modifies`/keep must be justified in a task note, else it is feedback.

DECISION — NEW requirement, not an extension [with user — the brief delegated the call]. `requirements.requirement.plan-coverage-scoped-to-change-set-delta` describes the BINARY's coverage scope computation, realised by `solution.component.plan-coverage-check` and implemented-by Rust functions (`rust.apg.plan_cmd.verify.*`). The agent behaviour is a DIFFERENT implementation surface — the product-source prompt `opencode-suite/agents/plan-review.md` (a scanned `docs` File) — so extending the existing requirement would either falsely widen `plan-coverage-check`'s `implemented-by` set onto an md file or leave the prompt uncovered. A separate requirement keeps the spine honest and maps coverage 1:1 to the edited prompt.

NEW NODES. `requirements.user.plan-review-agent` ⊃ `requirements.requirement.plan-review-deterministic-and-minimal` (feature `plan-coverage`, same change-set) —drives→ `domain.entity.plan-review-verdict` (new entity under `domain.group.plan-verification`) —realised-by→ `solution.component.plan-review-prompt` (under `solution.container.opencode-suite`) —implemented-by→ `opencode-suite/agents/plan-review.md` (a real File FQN, so the edit is a `modifies` over existing code; no planned node).

BOUNDARY WIDENING. `requirements.constraint.plan-coverage-change-boundary` (attached to `plan-coverage-scoped-to-change-set-delta`) is widened so the agent-prompt reconciliation is IN scope; the binary surfaces it already excluded (realization gate, feedback gate, durable write surface, suite tools, `apg plan verify` CLI/exit) stay out.

RELATION TO THE EXISTING RULE. The deterministic pass consumes the binary's delta verdict (`domain.entity.plan-coverage`); the semantic pass enforces the same less-code direction that clause 3 of `plan-coverage-scoped-to-change-set-delta` already encodes on the coverage side — a removed solution node / `implemented-by` edge leaves its code FQN in scope, so a task must touch it, normally a `deletes` — and turns it into reviewable feedback.

PLAN FOLLOW-UP (plan-writer, not authored here): every requirement must be Satisfied by exactly one phase, so the plan must add a `Satisfies` for `requirements.requirement.plan-review-deterministic-and-minimal`.
